categories.main_business_segments: Expedia Group operates through three main business segments: Retail, B2B, and trivago. The Retail segment includes consumer-facing brands such as Expedia.com, Hotels.com, Vrbo, Orbitz, Travelocity, and others, offering a wide range of travel and advertising services. The B2B segment, primarily Expedia Partner Solutions, provides travel products and technology to third-party businesses, including airlines, travel agents, and financial institutions. The trivago segment operates a hotel metasearch platform generating advertising revenue by referring users to travel service providers.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Expedia leverages a unified technology platform, integrating proprietary systems for booking, customer service, data analytics, and supplier connectivity. The company utilizes cloud computing, AI-driven customer service tools, and a shared infrastructure for transaction processing, search, and fraud prevention. Continuous investment in platform migration and modernization enables scalable, efficient operations and rapid product innovation across brands.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Expedia serves leisure and unmanaged business travelers globally through its consumer brands, as well as travel suppliers (hotels, airlines, property owners) and business partners (corporate travel managers, financial institutions) via its B2B offerings. Key end markets include lodging (hotels and alternative accommodations), air travel, car rentals, cruises, and travel insurance, with a focus on both individual consumers and enterprise partners.
categories.geographic_coverage: Expedia operates worldwide, with significant presence in the United States, Europe, Asia-Pacific, and other international markets. Its brands and platforms are localized for numerous countries, and the company maintains offices and customer service centers in over 50 countries. The U.S. remains the largest market, but international operations are a major source of growth and revenue.
categories.supply_chain_position: Expedia acts as an intermediary (midstream) in the travel supply chain, connecting travel suppliers (hotels, airlines, property owners) with end customers through its online platforms. It does not own travel inventory but facilitates bookings, payments, and distribution for suppliers, while also providing technology and distribution solutions to other businesses.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Expedia's strategic focus is on leveraging its unified technology platform to drive operational efficiency, product innovation, and improved traveler experiences. Key initiatives include consolidating loyalty programs into a single global platform, increasing direct customer relationships and app adoption, expanding alternative accommodations, and enhancing B2B offerings. The company invests heavily in technology, data science, and AI to support scalable growth and differentiation.
categories.revenue_model: Expedia generates revenue primarily through three models: the merchant model (Expedia is the merchant of record and collects payment from travelers), the agency model (Expedia acts as an agent and earns commissions from suppliers), and the advertising model (revenue from advertising and media placements, especially via trivago). In 2022, merchant, agency, and advertising/media/other accounted for 66%, 26%, and 8% of total revenue, respectively.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Expedia faces intense competition from global online travel agencies (OTAs) such as Booking Holdings (Booking.com, Priceline), Airbnb, Trip.com, and direct supplier channels (hotels, airlines), as well as metasearch engines (Google, Kayak, TripAdvisor) and emerging travel tech platforms. Expedia is one of the largest OTAs globally, with a broad portfolio and significant scale, but competes on price, supply breadth, technology, and customer experience.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2022, Expedia reported $11.7 billion in revenue, a 36% increase from 2021, reflecting strong recovery in travel demand post-pandemic. Gross bookings reached $95 billion, up 31% year-over-year. Adjusted EBITDA was $2.35 billion, and the company returned to profitability with net income of $352 million. Expedia maintains a large cash position and significant financial scale, with a focus on margin improvement and operational efficiency.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Expedia emphasizes its broad and deep travel supply, global brand portfolio, and unified technology platform as key differentiators. The company offers travelers a comprehensive selection of lodging, flights, and experiences, competitive pricing, and loyalty rewards, while providing suppliers and partners with advanced distribution, technology, and marketing solutions. Its focus on innovation, customer experience, and multi-product offerings aims to drive higher engagement, repeat business, and long-term loyalty.
